findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores a Promise in `calendar` but its callers are not updated
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `getCalendarCredentials` returns items whose `calendar` field is a `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other consumer that reads `.calendar` directly will now hold a Promise, so a call like `calendar.listCalendars()` fails at runtime. The return type changed silently. Nothing in the diff checks the other call sites, such as the trpc calendars router, availability code and selected-calendar handling.

findings.title: All app imports are started eagerly at module load
findings.body: The object literal calls `import(...)` for all ~29 apps when `@calcom/app-store` is first loaded. Every app module, with its heavy dependencies (googleapis, stripe, zoom, etc.), is therefore loaded immediately and unconditionally. This defeats the purpose of async or lazy loading. To be lazy, the values should be thunks, such as `() => import(...)`, resolved only on demand. Any app whose import throws or rejects at load time also creates an unhandled rejection at module init, even if that app is never used.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes the try/catch ineffective and the deletes unawaited
findings.body: The `forEach` callback is now `async`, so the returned promises are discarded and the surrounding `try/catch` can no longer catch their errors. A failure in `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The code also proceeds to send emails and return before the calendar and video deletions finish, which is risky in serverless environments where the process can end early. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead. The same problem is duplicated in `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` and in `trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`.

findings.title: Async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, `forEach(async ...)` awaits `getCalendar` and then `deleteEvent`. `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` therefore runs after the outer flow has continued to `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`. Before this PR the callback had no `await` before the first push, so it ran synchronously up to the first `deleteEvent`. The awaited `getCalendar` now guarantees the callback yields first. The calendar deletions are neither awaited nor reliably included in `apiDeletes`, and their errors are unhandled. Recurring cancellations may not delete the calendar events before the response returns. Use `for...of` with `await`, or collect promises with `map` and `Promise.all`.

findings.title: calendar promises are created eagerly and rejections are handled late
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` calls `getCalendar` immediately for each credential and keeps the promises. They are only awaited later, inside the `getConnectedCalendars` try/catch. If a promise rejects before it is awaited, or if the caller never calls `getConnectedCalendars`, this is an unhandled rejection.
